outline: 1133 Area of a Triangle using Trigonometry

examples.solution_text:
Two sides and their included angle are known. Use the cosine rule to find the third side; there is no complete opposite pair for the sine rule.

$\begin{aligned}x^2&=10^2+15^2-2(10)(15)\cos60^{\circ}\\x&=\sqrt{175}\\x&\approx13.2\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

The side $BC$ and its opposite angle $A$ form a complete pair. Use the sine rule; $AC$ is opposite $45^{\circ}$.

$\begin{aligned}\frac{AC}{\sin45^{\circ}}&=\frac{14}{\sin75^{\circ}}\\AC&=\frac{14\sin45^{\circ}}{\sin75^{\circ}}\\AC&\approx10.2\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

All three sides are known. Use the cosine rule for an angle, placing the opposite side $12$ in the subtracted term.

$\begin{aligned}\cos\theta&=\frac{8^2+10^2-12^2}{2(8)(10)}\\\cos\theta&=\frac{20}{160}\\\theta&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{20}{160}\right)\\\theta&\approx82.8^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

The side $9$ and its opposite angle $55^{\circ}$ form a complete pair. Use the sine rule with sine on top.

$\begin{aligned}\frac{\sin B}{6}&=\frac{\sin55^{\circ}}{9}\\\sin B&=\frac{6\sin55^{\circ}}{9}\\B&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{6\sin55^{\circ}}{9}\right)\\B&\approx33.1^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

Use the acute value requested.

Two sides and their included angle are known. Use the SAS area rule.

$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac12ab\sin C\\&=\frac12(12)(16)\sin65^{\circ}\\&\approx87.0\text{ cm}^2\end{aligned}$

First use the cosine rule with the two sides and included angle.

$\begin{aligned}AC^2&=15^2+10^2-2(15)(10)\cos50^{\circ}\\AC&=\sqrt{325-300\cos50^{\circ}}\\AC&\approx11.5\text{ cm}\end{aligned}$

Keep the full calculator value $d=\sqrt{325-300\cos50^{\circ}}$. The pair $AC$ and $50^{\circ}$ now allows the sine rule.

$\begin{aligned}\frac{\sin A}{10}&=\frac{\sin50^{\circ}}{d}\\A&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{10\sin50^{\circ}}{d}\right)\\A&\approx42^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

The supplementary value would make the angle sum exceed $180^{\circ}$.

Find the angle $C$ between the $10\text{ m}$ and $13\text{ m}$ sides using the cosine rule.

$\begin{aligned}\cos C&=\frac{10^2+13^2-17^2}{2(10)(13)}\\C&=\cos^{-1}\left(-\frac1{13}\right)\\C&=94.4117\ldots^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

Use this unrounded angle in the area rule.

$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac12(10)(13)\sin C\\&\approx64.8\text{ m}^2\end{aligned}$

Find the third angle, then use the sine rule to obtain a second side.

$\begin{aligned}C&=180^{\circ}-50^{\circ}-70^{\circ}\\C&=60^{\circ}\\\frac{AC}{\sin70^{\circ}}&=\frac{40}{\sin60^{\circ}}\\AC&=\frac{40\sin70^{\circ}}{\sin60^{\circ}}\end{aligned}$

The sides $AB$ and $AC$ enclose $50^{\circ}$. Use the unrounded side in the area rule.

$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac12(40)\left(\frac{40\sin70^{\circ}}{\sin60^{\circ}}\right)\sin50^{\circ}\\&\approx665\text{ m}^2\end{aligned}$

The back bearing of $A$ from $B$ is $225^{\circ}$. Hence the included angle is

$\begin{aligned}\angle ABC&=225^{\circ}-120^{\circ}\\&=105^{\circ}.\end{aligned}$

Use the cosine rule.

$\begin{aligned}AC^2&=40^2+65^2-2(40)(65)\cos105^{\circ}\\AC&=\sqrt{5825-5200\cos105^{\circ}}\\AC&\approx85\text{ km}\end{aligned}$

Both bearings are measured from the same north line at $O$.

$\begin{aligned}\angle POQ&=115^{\circ}-35^{\circ}\\&=80^{\circ}.\end{aligned}$

Use the two sides and this included angle in the area rule.

$\begin{aligned}A&=\frac12(20)(28)\sin80^{\circ}\\&\approx275.7\text{ km}^2\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: Cosine rule gives x²=100+225−300cos60°=175; x=13.228756… cm, hence 13.2 cm. Diagram side proportions and included angle agree.
AC=14sin45°/sin75°=10.248711… m, hence 10.2 m. Corrected coordinates produce the stated 75° and 45° angles.
cosθ=(64+100−144)/160=0.125; θ=82.819244…°, hence 82.8°. The marked angle is opposite the 12 cm side.
sinB=6sin55°/9; B=33.099959…°, hence 33.1°. Its supplement cannot coexist with 55°. Corrected coordinates match the side ratio and angle.
Area=½(12)(16)sin65°=87.005547… cm², hence 87.0 cm². The given angle lies between the labelled sides.
AC=√(325−300cos50°)=11.496247… cm, hence 11.5 cm. Using the unrounded distance, A=asin(10sin50°/AC)=41.785439…°, hence 42°. The supplementary angle plus 50° exceeds 180°.
cosC=(100+169−289)/260=−1/13; C=94.411725…°. Area=65sinC=64.807406… m², hence 64.8 m². Diagram proportions match all three sides.
C=60° and AC=40sin70°/sin60°. Area=½(40)(AC)sin50°=664.965537… m², hence 665 m². Diagram angles and the selected included angle agree.

Back bearing BA = 225°, so angle ABC = 225° − 120° = 105°. Independently calculated AC = sqrt(40² + 65² − 2×40×65×cos105°) = 84.6809248564 km, rounding to 85 km. The supplied source Q9 teaches bearing conversion followed by cosine rule. The side-label placement separates 40 km from 045° without changing coordinates, arcs, givens or font size.

Angle POQ = 115° − 35° = 80°. Independently calculated area = ½×20×28×sin80° = 275.7461708434 km², rounding to 275.7 km². The supplied source Q2 explicitly combines bearings and triangle area. Moving the 20 km label left preserves the geometry and bearing arcs while separating it from 035°.

Angle ABC = 105° and AC = 84.6809248564 km. Independently calculated angle ACB = arcsin(40×sin105°/AC) = 27.1464252295°. Its supplement is impossible with angle B = 105°. Back bearing CB = 300°; bearing CA = 300° − 27.1464252295° = 272.8535747705°, rounding to 273°T. This matches the cosine-rule, sine-rule and return-bearing sequence in source Q14. The repeated side-label repair preserves geometry; the solution angle annotation agrees with the calculation.
